column1: # The lines of the bash hooks and of the shims, mapped to a hook/ rule ID and the ref it guards
# ('-' for none), or to a notice/ ID and the fields it carries, read by scripts/lib/hook-parity.sh
# (ADR-0022). One row per line form: an extended regular expression matched against the whole
# line, the ID, and the fields, separated by tabs; a field names the groups of the pattern as \1
^pre-commit: refused — the checkout is on 'main', and changes reach main through a pull request
^pre-commit: refused — the checks are red on the resolved merge
^pre-merge-commit: refused — the checkout is on 'main', and changes reach main through a pull request
^pre-merge-commit: refused — the documentation check is red on the merge
^pre-push: refused — changes reach main through a pull request, not a push
^pre-push: refused — the checks are red, and they pass before anything is pushed

^pre-push: (.+) carries ([0-9]+) draft ADR\(s\); they take their numbers on the branch of the pull request into main, by scripts/ready-for-main\.sh \((README|CONTRIBUTING\.md), Integration branches, step 7\)\.$
^pre-push: the checks passed on this tree before; not run again\.$

^reference-transaction: refused — main moves only to what origin/main has, and changes reach it through a pull request \(AGENTS\.md, section 6\)\. Take up the remote's main: git merge --ff-only origin/main$

^reference-transaction: refused — main moves only to what origin/main has, and changes reach it through a pull request \(AGENTS\.md, section 6\)\. main has commits origin/main lacks; keep them on a branch and take main back: git switch -c feat/<topic> main, then git branch -f main origin/main$
